name: Assimilatory Nitrate Reduction
notes: Assimilatory pathway for nitrogen acquisition: nitrate → nitrite → ammonia. Used for biosynthesis (amino acids, nucleotides), not respiration. Distinguished from dissimilatory reduction by enzyme types and cellular location.

genes.name: ferredoxin-nitrate reductase
genes.notes: Assimilatory nitrate reductase using ferredoxin. Alternative to NR and nasAB.

genes.name: nitrate reductase (NAD(P)H)
genes.notes: NAD(P)H-dependent nitrate reductase. Alternative to narB and nasAB.

genes.name: assimilatory nitrate reductase catalytic subunit
genes.notes: Catalytic subunit of two-component nitrate reductase.

genes.name: assimilatory nitrate reductase electron transfer subunit
genes.notes: Electron transfer subunit of two-component nitrate reductase.

genes.name: two-component assimilatory nitrate reductase
genes.notes: Two-subunit assimilatory nitrate reductase. Alternative to single-subunit narB and NR.

genes.name: nitrite reductase (NAD(P)H)
genes.notes: NAD(P)H-dependent nitrite reductase. Alternative to nirA.

genes.name: ferredoxin-nitrite reductase
genes.notes: Ferredoxin-dependent nitrite reductase. Alternative to NIT-6.

assimilatory_nitrate.name: Assimilatory Nitrate Reduction
assimilatory_nitrate.notes: Two-step pathway for nitrogen assimilation. Step 1: nitrate → nitrite (narB, NR, or nasAB). Step 2: nitrite → ammonia (NIT-6 or nirA). All organisms need nitrogen for biosynthesis.

scoring.notes: Both steps required but many alternatives exist. Lower threshold since pathway is widespread with diverse enzyme variants.
